title: Run D-3: Co-doped MnSbSe
subtitle: Co-doped MnSbSe: make the sample → measure the optical gap and simulate → strained film
task: Dope MnSbSe with Co past the critical content where its crystal structure distorts. Deliver a pellet that is only the distorted phase, whose magnetic ordering temperature (where its magnetic order sets in) is 178.3 ± 3 K. On the way, work out what went wrong with the group's earlier pilot pellet. Then measure the pellet's optical gap and find the Hubbard U (an interaction strength in the DFT+U simulation) at which the simulation reproduces that gap. Include a k-point table that shows the simulation grid is fine enough. Finally predict and grow a strained film whose gap is 0.79 ± 0.04 eV, and predict a second film's gap before measuring it. One budget of 62 lab actions covers all three stages; the agent works through a Linux desktop (GSAS-II, LibreOffice Calc, a text editor).

outcome.headline: Delivered the right pellet and optical gap. It named the wrong magnetic order for the strained film and ran out of budget before growing the second film.

failure.headline: The agent assumed the magnetic order it found at zero strain still held in the strained film. It reported the checkerboard antiferromagnetic order, but the stripe order has lower energy there. The budget then ran out before the second film could be grown

chain.text: Named the pilot pellet's cause (dopant loss) correctly, but cited no synthesis and XRD that tells the two possible causes apart
Cited a simulation at grid size n = 8, coarser than the converged grid, with no convergence table at its strain
Delivered U = 5.05 eV, with the checkerboard magnetic order (AFM-checker) as the lowest-energy order at zero strain, after 57 of 62 actions
Committed the device strain assuming AFM-checker. At that strain the stripe order is lower in energy
Optical measurement of the only film used the last budget (61 of 62)
Delivered film F001 with no second film

Segments run in order. Close each one with lab__deliver(segment, item, answer). The answer is frozen

steps.say: Analyzing S001/S002 patterns the same way.
S001 shows split (200)/(020) → distorted phase, a_inplane ≈ 3.946 Å, x ≈ 0.177. Now S002.
S002: strongly split, a_inplane ≈ 3.935 Å → x ≈ 0.264. Now checking Tc from M(T).
S001 Tc ≈ 163 K (lower than P001's ~172 K). Checking S002.
S002 Tc ≈ 182 K. In the distorted phase Tc rises with x (~213 K per unit x), so 178.3 K needs x_actual ≈ 0.245. At 750 °C about 12% of the Co is lost, so I'll use nominal x = 0.278.
events: S003: dopant evaporated during the anneal (lost 0.036 in x)

steps.say: S003 Tc ≈ 178 K (S003's M(T) drop sits about 4 K below S002's). That is within 178.3 ± 3 K. Now its XRD.
S003 indexes as single-phase orthorhombic: a = 3.968 Å, b = 3.907 Å → a_inplane = 3.938 Å, c = 8.756 Å, which gives a Vegard x_actual of 0.245. Tc ≈ 178 K. Delivering segment A.
events: Delivered S003: true x = 0.242, distorted, single phase, ordering temperature 178.3 K
S003: true optical gap 0.683 eV; true effective U 5.05 eV

The Tauc fit gives a direct gap of 0.682 eV, and it holds steady across fit windows. Next I'll re-read the manual's DFT rules.
